title: Toplumsal Bellek ve Kültürel Kimlik Açısından Âşıklık Geleneği (Azerbaycan Örneği)
summary: This volume is centered on Prof. Dr. Hatire Beşirli’s research titled “The Tradition of the Âşık from the Perspectives of Social Memory and Cultural Identity (The Case of Azerbaijan)” and offers a comprehensive examination of the âşık tradition from historical, sociological, and cultural perspectives. The work examines a broad historical process—spanning from the ancient roots of the ozan-baksı tradition to today’s digitalized performance world—through an interdisciplinary lens. This book is not merely an academic study intended solely for folklore researchers. It is also a valuable reference source for any reader seeking to understand the cultural roots of the Turkic world, how its social memory has been shaped, and the cultural tools through which identity construction is sustained. Transcending the technical analysis of poetic forms to become a “cultural identity reading,” this work opens the doors to listening to the sound of the saz not only with the ear but also with historical consciousness and cultural awareness. The tradition of aşık poetry, which contributes to the understanding of the solid cultural foundations upon which future generations will build their own identities, once again demonstrates its enduring vitality and social significance that has persisted for centuries. In this context, the art of the aşık powerfully reminds us that the sound resonating through the saz’s strings is, in fact, the memory, identity, and historical continuity of a nation. Finally, we hope this study will inspire a deeper understanding of the shared cultural heritage of the Turkic world and spur new research on the tradition of the aşık.
